paragraphs.en: On 28 May, the last day, delegates of the Polish stamp societies met in Toruń. On Marian Niklewski's initiative they founded their national union and elected him its president. The Germans arrested Alfons on 6 March 1940. He died at Mauthausen-Gusen on 29 May 1941. Marian was held in Dachau. He came back and restarted the Toruń society on 8 July 1946.

paragraphs.en: On 24 September 1703 the heavy guns of the Swedish king Charles XII began to fire incendiary shells into the besieged town. One of them hit the town hall tower and set fire to the gunpowder stored in the attic. All roofs and the rooms above the ground floor burned. The brick walls survived. The tower never got back the tin spire it lost in that fire. In its lower part some bricks are still black from the smoke.

paragraphs.en: A legend says the town hall was built like a calendar. The 15-year-old Fryderyk Chopin repeated it in a letter of August 1825: as many windows as days in the year, as many halls as months. Small figures of old burghers stand in the windows, made after a Gothic painting from a Toruń church.
